own_solution.law: The field normal to the rail plane is B cos(theta). The motional emf is B L v cos(theta), giving current I = B L v cos(theta)/R and an opposing force along the rails of I L B cos(theta). Terminal balance gives mg sin(theta) = B^2 L^2 v cos^2(theta)/R, so v = mg R sin(theta)/(B^2 L^2 cos^2(theta)). With R = 0.5 ohm, v = 2.835648148 m/s. Adding 1.3 ohm in the rail circuit makes R = 1.8 ohm and v = 10.208333333 m/s.
assumptions: The rod remains horizontal across the rails, perpendicular to their downhill direction.
The stated uniform magnetic field is prescribed.
The lamp's separately powered circuit has no coupling to the rail circuit in the stated model.

defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T2332 and T2BCE replace the explicit 1.3 Ω specification used in the other resistor variants with 'small', violating the requirement that variants retain the same stated number and unit.

notes: The base physics and all six individual renderings have unique terminal speeds. The invalid verdict concerns the required matching of variant quantities: T2332 versus TE145 and T2BCE versus T88DE change numerical specificity as well as wording. Resistors used only in an earlier run are disconnected from the present terminal-speed calculation. The unspecified resistance in the lamp circuit also does not affect the answer.
